findings.evidence: Current contract.md:294 reads: "17. `dotnet msbuild src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/AgentGuard.Boundaries.csproj -getItem:ProjectReference` returns exactly two project references: `AgentGuard.Abstractions` and `AgentGuard.Analyzers`. The analyzer reference has `OutputItemType=Analyzer` and `ReferenceOutputAssembly=false`." `git diff -- .dev/inprocess/74-pre-work-move-system-services/contract.md` shows this replaced the checkpointed (HEAD/a12e58b) wording verbatim: "17. `dotnet msbuild src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/AgentGuard.Boundaries.csproj -getItem:ProjectReference` returns `AgentGuard.Abstractions` and nothing else." I grepped the whole Decisions section (contract.md lines 3-135, including all five dated 'Recorded conversation authorizations' entries at lines 128-132) for 'Acceptance 17', 'ProjectReference', and 'getItem' and every match returns empty — no quoted Tim decision records this specific edit, though roughly twenty other substantive changes in the same section each carry one. The only traces of the change are agent-side: implement-output.json's own hedge ("READ THIS BEFORE RULING... I rule it met on that basis... a reviewer can rule otherwise without rediscovering it") and readiness-output.json's unbacked assertion ("Tim's Acceptance 17 edit IS live at line 275") — neither is a contract record, and READINESS's own DECISION-check standard (per rails-run-a-workflow) states "approval quoted in a prompt or a prior agent's output is not a record; only the contract counts." On the merits the corrected text is actually true and more rigorous than the original: I independently re-ran `dotnet msbuild src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/AgentGuard.Boundaries.csproj -getItem:ProjectReference` myself and got exactly two entries (AgentGuard.Analyzers, OutputItemType=Analyzer/ReferenceOutputAssembly=false, DefiningProjectFullPath=Directory.Build.props; and AgentGuard.Abstractions) — the original 'nothing else' wording was never satisfiable even before this relocation, since Directory.Build.props injects the Analyzer reference into every project in the repo. This is not a cheat that weakens the check's substance, but it is a governing-requirement edit with no Decisions-section provenance.

findings.summary: tdd-result.md's Acceptance-19 evidence row (line 153, part of the finished change's own CHANGED_FILES) cites `dry-fix-scope-and-digests.txt` as one of three files proving `git diff --check` returned EXIT=0, but that file contains no `git diff --check` invocation and no `EXIT=` output anywhere — the citation is fabricated/unbacked, a Rail 6 (stale-or-unused-data) violation: a conclusion presented as independently corroborated by a live check that the named source never ran.
findings.evidence: tdd-result.md:153 reads verbatim: "| 19 | `git diff --check` passes; ... | ... | analyzer-behavioral | false | `git diff --check` EXIT=0 in `tdd-acceptance25-scope-and-digests.txt`, `tdd-correction-diff-check.txt` and `dry-fix-scope-and-digests.txt`. ... |". I read the full 193-line `dry-fix-scope-and-digests.txt` and ran `grep -c 'diff --check'` (result 0) and `grep -c 'EXIT'` (result 0) against it directly — zero matches anywhere in the file. Its actual content (confirmed by direct read) is a before/after digest table, `git diff --stat`, `git status --porcelain`, and a pasted per-file `diff -u -r`; its own sibling manifest file `dry-fix-commands-and-exits.txt:22-27` self-describes it as "digests before and after, git status, and the diff of this round alone" — no mention of `git diff --check`. The two OTHER cited files do legitimately contain it (`tdd-acceptance25-scope-and-digests.txt:5-6` = "$ git diff --check" / "EXIT=0"; `tdd-correction-diff-check.txt` = "git diff --check EXIT=0" verbatim), but both were captured in earlier rounds, before the DRY-fix round added its own new files (including `dry-fix-scope-and-digests.txt` and `tdd-acceptance25-mutation-proofs.txt`) to the index — so no evidence file shows `git diff --check` re-run fresh against the truly final, current tree. I independently re-ran `git diff --check` myself just now (bare form, matching the acceptance wording): EXIT=0, so the literal criterion still holds — but only the bare working-tree-vs-index form; `git diff HEAD --check` (working tree vs HEAD, which is what a full post-hoc audit of 'every contract boundary' would run) currently reports two whitespace violations, both confined to blank-context lines inside these same two pasted-diff evidence `.txt` files (a structural artifact of verbatim `diff -u` capture, not a code defect — no file under src/tests/analyzers is implicated).
findings.fix: Correct tdd-result.md:153's Acceptance-19 evidence: drop the false citation of `dry-fix-scope-and-digests.txt` (or add an actual `git diff --check` run to that file if it is meant to independently corroborate). Re-run `git diff --check` fresh against the current, final tree (after the DRY-fix round's own files are staged) and cite that live output instead of only carrying forward pre-DRY-fix-round captures. While re-running it, note for the record (not as a blocker, since it touches no shipped file) that `git diff --cached/HEAD --check` flags trailing whitespace at the blank-context lines inside `dry-fix-scope-and-digests.txt` and `tdd-acceptance25-mutation-proofs.txt` themselves — an artifact of pasting `diff -u` output verbatim, confined to process evidence files, with no code-file whitespace violation anywhere in `git diff --check`'s bare (Acceptance-19-literal) form.
